title: Review of c19's lattice-chemistry no-division negative: replicated on fresh seed 4 at both the default point and ky 0.08 km 0.4 (0 persistent splits; merges 2-3x splits; ringed cells coarsen into a near-static array); Supported
summary: I looked at pack_km04/sheet.png and the four screens, then ran the sighting's world.py (the world this finding uses) with labkit on seed 4 at 128^2 for 20000 steps, once with WORLD_P ky 0.08, km 0.4 (the finding's pack setting) and once at the default point. km 0.4: ~130 small ringed cells and rods form from noise by t~800 and coarsen by fusion to 46 by t=20000 (rerun/km04_seed4/sheet.png); labkit 99 splits, 0 persistent, 204 merges, 161 nucleations, max 1.1 body lengths. Default: 161 -> 60 cells, 60 splits, 0 persistent, 170 merges. In both, after t~5000 the array barely changes, as the finding describes, so the population sits at a carrying capacity without a growth-division cycle.

observations.D: rerun/km04_seed4/FACTS.md: 0 persistent of 99 splits, 204 merges, 133 -> 46 components; rerun/default_seed4/FACTS.md: 0 of 60, 170 merges; sheets t=5000-20000: near-static arrays of ringed cells and rods

controls_run.D: the default point on the same seed beside the ky 0.08 km 0.4 setting

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and two of the five settings, 20000 steps each; the negative covers this neighbourhood of parameters, not the lattice-chemistry class (an external death or a moving resource is untested).
